description: Historical full-package GPU build definitions. The 1.77 stable Windows desktop ships ONNX Runtime DirectML and CPU. Its optional NVIDIA worker is provisioned from core/accelerator_win64.json. The ROCm and XPU definitions are preview recipes, not published managed packs.

variants.name: cuda
requires: NVIDIA display driver with CUDA 12.4 support
variants.notes: Historical CUDA build reference for the stable Windows asset name. release.yml now builds the DirectML desktop. Compatible NVIDIA devices can install the separate per-user inference pack.

variants.name: rocm
variants.torch_sha256_note: AMD's Windows preview index does not publish a per-wheel SHA-256; the HTTPS URL is pinned but the download is not hash-verified.
hardware: AMD Radeon GPU listed in AMD's ROCm on Windows compatibility matrix
requires: Python 3.12 embedded runtime (the AMD wheel is cp312-only)
variants.notes: AMD ships Windows ROCm PyTorch wheels only for CPython 3.12 (torch 2.9.1 at the time of writing), matching the Python 3.12 desktop runtime as a separate ROCm PyTorch build rather than a drop-in swap in the DirectML stable bundle. HIP exposes the torch.cuda API, so the existing inference device contract can use it, but no AMD hardware has run it in CI. The bundle must collect rocm_sdk and _rocm_sdk_* because torch/lib itself contains only 13 DLLs.

variants.name: xpu
hardware: Intel Arc / Intel Core Ultra integrated GPU
requires: Intel graphics driver supported by the XPU wheel
Intel GPU exposed as torch.xpu by torch 2.9.1+xpu
variants.notes: Official cp312 Windows XPU wheels exist. The shared core.torch_backend contract now resolves torch.xpu, uses torch.xpu.mem_get_info for VRAM admission and synchronizes XPU work, so this is a real Python 3.12 preview build. No Intel GPU has run it in CI; Conv3d/SDPA and the bundled model remain unverified on XPU.
